name: TreodeDB
tagline: Replicated, sharded key-value store with multi-row atomic writes for REST services; abandoned in 2015.
description: TreodeDB was a distributed key-value store written in Scala by Treode, Inc. It replicated and sharded data across a cluster and offered conditional batch writes, multi-row atomic updates guarded by read timestamps, which let REST services extend optimistic concurrency through caches and CDNs using ETag-style versions. It kept versioned data and could feed Spark RDDs, DStreams and Hadoop InputFormats for analytics. Only 0.1 and 0.2 releases shipped (2014); commits ended in late 2015 and the company domain has lapsed. It remains a readable example of a transactional, versioned KV design.
statusNote: Last release 0.2.0 (Dec 2014) and last commit Oct 2015; Treode's domain has lapsed. Consider FoundationDB or TiKV.

scale.notes: Designed for sharding and replication but never proven at scale before development stopped.

strengths: Multi-row atomic writes with optimistic concurrency, unusual for a KV store of its time
Versioned data designed to work with HTTP caches and CDNs
Connectors for Spark and Hadoop analytics
weaknesses: No community, packages or documentation site still online
useCases: Studying conditional batch writes and versioned KV design
Reference Scala code for a replicated, sharded store
